newsitem.title: USA: Boeing merger may boost local economies - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Boeing merger may boost local economies - analysts.

text.p: Boeing Co's proposed acquisition of McDonnell Douglas Corp could provide a boost to the southern California economy and benefit Washington state, analysts said on Monday.
The combined firm, to be based at Boeing's headquarters in Seattle and to operate under the Boeing Co name, was projected to have 1997 sales of about $48 billion, and employ about 200,000 people.
Municipal analysts said the planned merger could benefit several local economies, particularly Long Beach, Calif., and the Seattle-area.

"You're looking at a giant aerospace presence that could potentially benefit all geographic locations where it has operations," said Chris Irwin, a director at U.S. credit rating agency Standard & Poor's Corp.

For Long Beach, located just south of Los Angeles, the merger could provide a "noticeable" economic boost within 18 months, according to Ted Gibson, chief economist for the California Department of Finance.
McDonnell Douglas currently has about 20,000 workers in Long Beach, just south of Los Angeles.
"We depend heavily on McDonnell Douglas as our largest employer," Long Beach Mayor Beverly O'Neill said. "This (merger) will strengthen their presence."
"This is a real plus for the economy, for the workers and for the city of Long Beach," she added.
For Washington state's economy, analysts said the acquisition could also hold rewards.
"The economy of Washington state has tended to swing with aircraft and parts," said Dennis Fusco, chief economist at the Washington State Department of Employment Security.
The aircraft and parts industry constitutes about one-quarter of all manufacturing jobs in Washington state, with total payrolls of over $4 billion, Fusco said.
Fusco said the Seattle-area along with the rest of the state should benefit from the acquisition. "Overall, I would view it (the merger) as a positive for the state," Fusco said.
